# contentful_locale (Resource)

Manages a Contentful Locale in a space's environment. The locale code identifies localized content; Contentful generates a separate system ID. Destroying a locale permanently deletes its localized content. Contentful rejects deletion of the default locale or a locale used as a fallback.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "contentful_locale" "example" {
  space_id       = var.contentful_space_id
  environment_id = var.contentful_environment_id

  name          = "German"
  code          = "de-DE"
  fallback_code = "en-US"
  optional      = true
}
```

## Required localized fields

When publishing all locales together, a fallback does not satisfy required-field validation. Set `optional = true` on a nondefault locale to allow publication with incomplete translations. Setting `optional = true` does not relax required default-locale values. See Contentful's [optional locale guidance](https://www.contentful.com/developers/docs/tutorials/general/setting-locales/#optional-locales); the setting is [unavailable for locale-based publishing](https://www.contentful.com/help/localization/manage-locales/).

## Manage existing and default locales

Import existing locales; creating the same code does not adopt them. Find system IDs with the [Locale data sources](../guides/existing-configuration), or generate import configuration with the [Locale list resource](../list-resources/locale). Review flags and fallback before applying: omitted flags take the resource defaults, and an omitted fallback clears it. After an ambiguous creation error, check Contentful and import an unrecorded locale before retrying.

Terraform tracks each locale by space, environment, and system ID. Changing its code updates that entity in place; it does not move the read-only `default` status to another entity. In a two-resource code swap, identities and content values stay with their original Terraform resources while code labels change. Stage the swap through an unused code, subject to Contentful's allowance; it is not atomic.

Review code-dependent Entry/Asset configurations, Content Type defaults, and clients before renaming. Content Management API (CMA) responses relabel existing values without advancing content versions or republishing. Verify Content Delivery API (CDA) and Content Preview API (CPA) responses separately: delivery and creation validation have been observed using older configurations after successful CMA updates.

Use [`prevent_destroy`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/lifecycle#prevent_destroy) to reject default-locale destruction or replacement while that rule remains configured. To stop managing it, use a [`removed` block with `destroy = false`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) (Terraform 1.7 or later).

## Manage fallback dependencies

The example requires an existing `en-US` locale. For two managed locales, reference the target's `code`, such as `fallback_code = contentful_locale.base.code`, to establish creation/deletion order.

Changing a referenced target's code requires staged applies:

1. Clear or redirect dependent fallbacks and apply.
2. Change the target's code and apply.
3. Reconnect the fallbacks and apply.

Also clear dependent fallbacks before disabling delivery; see Contentful's [fallback guidance](https://www.contentful.com/developers/docs/tutorials/general/setting-locales/).

## Disable or delete a locale

Disabling delivery hides nondefault translations from CDA/CPA; disabling editing hides them from CMA Entry/Asset reads. Locale entities remain discoverable. Disabling alone preserves content, but writing back visible fields while editing is disabled can delete hidden translations. Re-enable editing before content updates that must preserve them.

Deletion permanently removes translations and can remove Entry locale publication status even without field values under that code. Recreating the code gives a new identity and restores neither content nor publication metadata.

## Schema

### Required

- `code` (String) Locale code, for example `en-US`. Changing it updates the locale in place and affects subsequent content API responses. Contentful rejects a code change while another locale uses it as a fallback.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment containing the locale. Use a concrete environment ID for a stable management target. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `name` (String) Name of the locale.
- `space_id` (String) ID of the space containing the locale. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `content_delivery_api` (Boolean) Whether localized content is included in Content Delivery API and Content Preview API responses. Defaults to true. Clear dependent fallbacks before disabling delivery.
- `content_management_api` (Boolean) Whether localized content is available through the Content Management API and for editing in the web app. Disabling it hides localized Entry and Asset fields from management reads and rejects writes containing that code; the Locale entity remains discoverable. Defaults to true.
- `fallback_code` (String) Code of an existing locale to use when translated content is missing. Fallback chains cannot contain cycles. Omission sends null to clear the fallback; an empty string is sent unchanged for Contentful to validate.
- `optional` (Boolean) Whether required localized fields may be empty for this locale when publishing all locales together. This does not relax required fields in the default locale. Defaults to false.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `default` (Boolean) Whether this is the environment's default locale. Contentful does not allow changing this status.
- `id` (String) Composite Terraform resource identifier in `space_id/environment_id/locale_id` form.
- `locale_id` (String) System ID generated by Contentful, distinct from the locale code.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Choose one of the following methods. Match the resource address and Contentful IDs to your configuration, then review the plan before applying.

### Import by identity

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with `identity`:

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    space_id       = var.contentful_space_id
    environment_id = var.contentful_environment_id
    locale_id      = var.contentful_locale_id
  }
  to = contentful_locale.example
}
```

### Import by ID

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with `id`:

```terraform
import {
  id = "${var.contentful_space_id}/${var.contentful_environment_id}/${var.contentful_locale_id}"
  to = contentful_locale.example
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `locale_id` (String)
